explanations: terra: God makes earth فِرَاشًا, heaven بِنَاءً, and rain-produced fruit provision, constructing the world as one furnished room of floor, roof, water, and food.

luna: The section's secondary sense of لَاغِيَة as something omitted from account has a Quranic counterpart: God does not hold people to account for لَغْو oaths. | terra: God does not take people to account for ٱللَّغْوِ in their oaths, supplying the section's bridge from speech excluded by hearing to what is excluded from reckoning.
terra: Everything in heaven and earth submits willingly or unwillingly and is returned to God, explicitly uniting the two modes of bending with the one final return.

luna: Faces on that Day are divided between brightness and darkness, repeating the section's paired faces and their opposed outcomes. | terra: The Day when faces whiten and blacken supplies another explicit division of humanity by the state written on the face.

luna: The bright-faced group is in God's mercy, specifying the garden side of the section's two faces on that Day. | terra: The whitened faces remain in God's mercy, completing the favorable side of the contrast begun in 3:106.
luna: The section names the ح س ب root in its sufficiency sense; this verse says “Allah is sufficient for us,” alongside reliance on Him.
terra: وَكَفَىٰ بِٱللَّهِ حَسِيبًا fuses “sufficient” and “reckoner” in the compact wording behind the section's dictionary bridge.
terra: Whoever turns away from the Messenger is told that he was not sent as a keeper over them, matching turning away with the absence of control.

luna: Here too the oath's لَغْو is not charged, while deliberate oaths are; this makes the section's link between idle speech and what is left out of account concrete. | terra: لَا يُؤَاخِذُكُمُ ٱللَّهُ بِٱللَّغْوِ repeats the unaccounted oath sense and then distinguishes deliberate oaths that do count.
terra: Those deceived by nearer life receive boiling water and painful punishment for their disbelief, joining the punitive drink to failed response to reminder.
luna: This verse commands looking at fruit as it forms and ripens, joining the section's gaze at created earth to food growing from it.
terra: Insights have come from the Lord; whoever sees does so for himself, and the Prophet says he is not a guardian, joining sight to the limit on his role.

terra: On the common camel reading of ٱلْجَمَلُ, those too proud for the signs cannot enter the garden until it passes through a needle's eye; the contemplated camel becomes the measure of excluded entry.
terra: Hell becomes an inverted room: its bed is Jahannam and above it are غَوَاشٍ, coverings of fire; this immediately follows the camel-and-garden boundary in 7:40.

luna: The section says rain's revival of earth proves resurrection; this verse sends water to a dead land, then says God will likewise bring out the dead. | terra: Rain revives dead land and كَذَٰلِكَ نُخْرِجُ ٱلْمَوْتَىٰ states that bringing forth the dead follows the same visible pattern.
luna: The same root's sufficiency sense appears in “Allah is sufficient for you,” distinct from its accounting use in the section's final verse.
terra: People are told to work; God, the Messenger, and believers will see the work, then all return to the Knower who reports it, joining labor, sight, message, and return.
luna: The Messenger says “Allah is sufficient for me,” a further Quranic use of the section's named root in its sufficiency sense.
terra: All return to God; He repeats creation to repay justly, while disbelievers receive boiling drink, joining return, recreation, accounting, and infernal water.
terra: The nearer life is likened to rain mingling with earth's food for people and livestock before the adorned ground is suddenly reaped bare.
luna: Those who do good receive more and have no dust or humiliation on their faces, a specific reversal of the section's punished faces.

luna: The section's face-covering punishment has a dark counterpart: faces are covered as if with pieces of night, and their owners are people of the Fire. | terra: Dark pieces of night seem to have أُغْشِيَتْ وُجُوهُهُمْ, another Judgment image in which covering settles directly upon faces.
luna: Every soul is returned to God and confronted with what it did, directly joining the section's return to its accounting.
terra: The question whether the Prophet would compel people to become believers defines the same boundary expressed by لَّسْتَ عَلَيْهِم بِمُصَيْطِرٍ.
terra: Truth has come from the Lord; guidance benefits the hearer, straying harms him, and the Prophet is not a trustee over them.
terra: Food provisions, an added camel-load, and an easy measure occur together, an indirect meeting of camel, sustenance, and measured sufficiency.
terra: The missing royal cup is linked to a promised camel-load of grain, bringing cup, camel, and measure together in a non-eschatological scene.

luna: The section links its opening al-Ghāshiya to later punishment; this verse names a غَاشِيَةٌ of God's punishment and the Hour's sudden arrival. | terra: A غَاشِيَةٌ مِّنْ عَذَابِ ٱللَّهِ places the section's opening cover beside punishment and asks whether people feel secure from its arrival.
terra: Immediately after the covering punishment of 12:107, the Prophet identifies his way as calling to God عَلَىٰ بَصِيرَةٍ, adding the messenger and lucid sight to that warning.

luna: The heavens are raised without visible pillars, repeating the section's invitation to look at how the sky was raised. | terra: God raised the heavens without visible pillars and explains the signs so people may be certain of meeting their Lord; the viewed sky proves the awaited meeting.

luna: The earth is spread with mountains, rivers, and varied growth, echoing the section's sequence of sky, mountain, and earth. | terra: The One who spread the earth, placed mountains, and made paired fruits follows the raised sky of 13:2, closely paralleling the section's sequence of created objects.
terra: All in heaven and earth prostrate willingly or unwillingly, as do their shadows morning and evening, joining voluntary and compelled lowering to the daily outward-and-homeward rhythm.

luna: Against the section's drink that passes easily, this drink is barely swallowed (وَلَا يَكَادُ يُسِيغُهُ); thirst relief itself becomes torment. | terra: The condemned gulps the drink but وَلَا يَكَادُ يُسِيغُهُ; this is the exact swallowing reversal of the easily swallowed milk in 16:66.

luna: The section's named cover (root غ ش ي), faces, and fire meet in this verse: fire envelops their faces. | terra: The section explicitly gathers its covering, faces, and fire in وَتَغْشَىٰ وُجُوهَهُمُ ٱلنَّارُ: the fire itself covers their faces.
terra: Immediately after fire covers faces in 14:50, God repays every soul and is سَرِيعُ ٱلْحِسَابِ, joining the section's opening scene to its final accounting.
terra: The next ayah calls the disclosure a proclamation and warning so that people may remember, placing the messenger's reminder after covered faces and divine reckoning in 14:50-51.

luna: This verse spreads earth, sets firm mountains, and grows measured things, paralleling the section's earth-and-mountain inspection as deliberate creation. | terra: The earth is extended, mountains set in it, and every balanced growth produced, a compact parallel to the section's spread earth and erected mountains.
terra: Resentment is removed and the garden dwellers sit as brothers on couches facing one another, completing the social room suggested by arranged furnishings.
terra: No fatigue touches them and they are never expelled, reversing the exhausted labor and unstable nearer-world lodging.

luna: Livestock are created for warmth and practical benefits, specifying the usefulness behind the section's invitation to look at the camel. | terra: Created livestock provide warmth, benefits, and food, anticipating the skins and fibers made into the earthly room in 16:80.

luna: The herds are beautiful when brought back in the evening and sent out in the morning, echoing the section's day's walk and evening return around the camel image. | terra: وَلَكُمْ فِيهَا جَمَالٌ حِينَ تُرِيحُونَ وَحِينَ تَسْرَحُونَ stages the herd's evening return and morning departure, concretizing the day's outward and homeward camel movement heard in the surah's ring.

luna: Livestock carry people and their burdens to distant lands, giving concrete travel use to the camel that opens the section's visual inquiry. | terra: Livestock carry loads to a land reachable only with hardship, giving the camel-language of advance and return its burdened road.
terra: Water descends from heaven as drink and produces the vegetation in which livestock graze, joining drink, pasture, and herd.
terra: The same water grows crops and fruits, extending the life-giving drink into human food.
luna: Firm mountains and paths are set on earth here, a specific parallel to the section's mountains erected and earth spread.

luna: This repeated sign says God sends water down and gives life to earth after its death, as in the section's explicit proof from revived soil. | terra: Rain gives dead earth life as a sign لِقَوْمٍ يَسْمَعُونَ, joining the life-giving water, earth, and hearing that the section sets against boiling water.

luna: The section contrasts the drinkers' easy passage of milk (سَائِغًا لِلشَّارِبِينَ) with Hell's barely swallowed drink; this verse names milk easy for drinkers. | terra: Milk brought from an animal's belly is سَائِغًا لِلشَّارِبِينَ, joining camel and drink while reversing the undrinkable draught of 14:17.

luna: The section's camel is livestock whose skins make homes and whose fibers furnish them; the verse makes worldly shelter and furnishings from animal materials. | terra: Livestock skins become portable houses and their wool, fur, and hair become furnishings, so the camel viewed in 88:17 supplies the earthly room mirrored by the furnished garden.
terra: After the portable houses of 16:80, God gives shade, mountain shelters, and protective garments, extending the earthly shelter that anticipates the garden room.

luna: The section says the Prophet does not keep the account; this verse gives each person an opened record on the Day of Resurrection. | terra: Each person's deed is fastened to him and a record is brought out on Resurrection spread open; 17:14 then makes him read and reckon it.

luna: The section names حِسَاب as its closing reckoning; here “enough for yourself today as accountant” (حَسِيبًا) joins the root's sufficiency and accounting senses. | terra: The person reads his own record and كَفَىٰ بِنَفْسِكَ ٱلْيَوْمَ عَلَيْكَ حَسِيبًا joins sufficiency language directly to the Day's accounting.
terra: The one who wants only the immediate life receives a measured portion and then Hell, opposing the Hereafter-directed striving appreciated in 17:19.
terra: Whoever desires the Hereafter and strives for it faithfully has that striving appreciated, the accepted counterpart to the laboring face whose effort does not save it.
luna: This verse calls the repentant “awwābīn”; it is another use of the section's word for a person who turns back to God.
terra: The condemned are gathered on their faces, blind, mute, and deaf, and their destination is Hell whose blaze is renewed.

luna: The section's boiling drink reverses life-giving rain: water like molten metal scalds faces (يَشْوِي الْوُجُوهَ) and is called a wretched drink. | terra: The water offered from the fire is like molten metal and يَشْوِى ٱلْوُجُوهَ, making water scorch faces instead of reviving dry ground.

luna: This verse answers 18:29's scalding drink with gardens, couches, silk, and ornaments, furnishing the garden counterpart developed in the section. | terra: After the face-scorching drink of 18:29, believers recline on adorned couches in gardens with flowing rivers, reproducing the section's two opposed rooms.
luna: Mountains are moved and earth exposed on the gathering Day, undoing the formed landscape the section asks the eye to inspect.

luna: This verse says no small or great deed is omitted from the opened record, repeating the section's link between its account and what is written. | terra: The laid-open record omits neither small nor great but enumerates it, while people find their deeds present before the just Lord.
terra: The question whether the Prophet should identify the greatest losers in deeds directs attention to labor whose apparent exertion fails.
terra: Their effort is lost in the nearer life while they think they are doing well, closely illuminating the section's laboring, exhausted face.
terra: Because they deny the signs and meeting with their Lord, their deeds collapse and receive no weight on Resurrection.

luna: The section's garden has no idle speech; this verse says they hear no لَغْو there, except a greeting of peace. | terra: The garden's inhabitants hear no لَغْوًا, only peace, while their provision comes morning and evening; hearing, empty speech, food, and the day's cycle meet.
terra: وَهَلْ أَتَىٰكَ حَدِيثُ مُوسَىٰ repeats the section's opening auditory question and begins a report that immediately turns to a seen fire.
terra: Moses sees a fire during the journey and hopes to bring a brand or guidance from it, moving from received report to sight within the neighboring ayah.
terra: The coming Hour is kept hidden so every soul may be repaid for what it strives, joining concealed timing, effort, and the Day's measure.

luna: Earth is made a bed here and water produces varied plants; that dwelling-floor and provision meet the section's world tent, soil, and garden. | terra: Earth is made a cradle with paths, rain descends, and paired plants emerge, building the habitable landscape that feeds people and herds.
luna: The question about what happens to mountains on the Day returns to the section's question of how they were set up.
luna: The mountains are crushed to dust, a direct reversal of their firm erection in the section's creation scene.
luna: The land is left level, with no crookedness or unevenness, reversing the section's spread earth as a prepared surface.

luna: The section says eyes lower and voices grow quiet; here voices humble themselves (خَشَعَتِ الْأَصْوَاتُ) and only a whisper is heard on that Day. | terra: On that Day voices are خَشَعَتِ ٱلْأَصْوَاتُ and only a whisper is heard, giving the section's covering Day its subdued soundscape.
terra: وَعَنَتِ ٱلْوُجُوهُ makes faces submit before the Living Sustainer, directly joining the face with involuntary lowliness on the Day.
terra: Humanity's حساب has drawn near while people remain heedless and turn away, bringing the final reckoning and the act of turning into one warning.
terra: No renewed reminder comes from their Lord without their hearing it at play, sharpening the section's contrast between hearing the report and treating it as empty sound.
terra: The question أَفَلَا يُؤْمِنُونَ follows the joining and opening of heaven and earth and the making of every living thing from water, turning visible creation toward belief.
terra: Firm mountains and broad paths are placed in earth after the water-and-creation sign, paralleling the section's viewed terrain.
terra: Heaven is made a protected roof, a direct world-room counterpart to the raised garden furnishings, though people turn from its signs.

luna: Scales of justice are set on the Day and no soul is wronged even by a mustard seed, making the section's account a precise measure. | terra: After the just scales are set for Resurrection, وَكَفَىٰ بِنَا حَاسِبِينَ makes the حساب root mean both reckoning and divine sufficiency.

luna: The section's revived earth is described here: barren land stirs and swells when rain falls, producing growth before the verse turns to resurrection. | terra: The long resurrection proof makes lifeless earth stir, swell, and grow after water descends, pairing human recreation with revived ground.
luna: This completes 22:5's earth scene by stating that God gives life to the dead; the section likewise makes revived ground evidence for the Last Day.
luna: After 22:5–6's revived soil and proof, this verse names the Hour and resurrection from graves, completing the section's inference from earth to the Day.

luna: The section's hot spring and fire meet the two disputing parties described here, one clothed in fire; the verse begins a punishment scene reversed by the garden. | terra: Garments of fire and boiling water poured over heads turn clothing and drink into the opposite of shelter and refreshment.

luna: This neighbor completes 22:19's fire scene: boiling water poured over heads melts what is in their bellies and their skins, matching the section's scalding-water imagery. | terra: The poured water melts what is inside bellies and skins, completing the bodily effect introduced in 22:19.
terra: Sacrificial camels are among God's signs; people are to mention God over them and then eat and feed others, joining camel, sign, and food.
terra: Travel through earth should yield hearts that understand and ears that hear; the ayah says blindness belongs to hearts, joining landscape, walking, sight, and hearing.

luna: Livestock provide drink from their bellies and food, closely joining the section's camel scene to the milk passed easily to drinkers. | terra: Livestock are explicitly a lesson: people are given drink from their bellies and receive many benefits and food from them.

luna: People are carried on livestock and ships, extending the section's camel from a created sign to a means of travel. | terra: Being carried on livestock and ships completes the animal lesson, giving the camel its journeying role beside its drink and materials.
terra: تَلْفَحُ وُجُوهَهُمُ ٱلنَّارُ makes the fire scorch faces, a direct parallel to the face-cooking water of 18:29.
terra: God creates every creature from water and gives different bodily forms of movement, a broader creation parallel that places the four-footed camel within water-made life.
luna: People return to God and are told what they did, echoing the section's pairing of return with account.
terra: When the Fire sees them from far away, they hear its raging and roaring, bringing sight, hearing, and fire into one Judgment scene.
terra: They are thrown bound into a narrow place within it, making punishment an oppressive room rather than an open, furnished one.
terra: Those gathered on their faces toward Hell are called worst in place and furthest from the way, making the lowered face the end of a misdirected journey.
terra: Whenever a fresh reminder comes, people turn away from it, directly joining reminder and the section's act of turning.
terra: They deny, so the reports of what they mocked will come to them, answering the opening question about whether the overwhelming report has arrived.
terra: When believers hear ٱللَّغْوَ they turn away from it, joining hearing, worthless speech, and a form of turning opposite to turning from the reminder.
terra: سِيرُوا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ فَٱنظُرُوا asks people to travel the earth and see how creation began, then states that God produces the final creation.
terra: Punishment covers the condemned from above and below while they are told to taste what they did, uniting enveloping punishment with recompensed labor.
terra: Believers who work righteousness are lodged in garden chambers beneath which rivers flow, joining accepted labor to the prepared room.
luna: This verse asks who sends rain and revives earth after its death, answering “God”; the section uses the same revived-earth sign to make resurrection perceptible.
terra: God brings living from dead, dead from living, revives earth, and says وَكَذَٰلِكَ تُخْرَجُونَ, aligning natural revival with human emergence.
terra: مُنِيبِينَ إِلَيْهِ is immediately joined to establishing prayer, bringing voluntary return and willing bodily worship together.

luna: It directly joins looking at God's mercy, earth revived after death, and God's reviving the dead, matching the section's eye-to-earth-to-resurrection movement. | terra: فَٱنظُرْ إِلَىٰٓ ءَاثَارِ رَحْمَتِ ٱللَّهِ commands a look at revived earth and concludes that its Reviver gives the dead life.

luna: The verse joins unsupported heavens, mountains, animals, and rain-grown plants, extending the section's look from landscape to living provision. | terra: One ayah gathers heavens raised without visible pillars, mountains set in earth, scattered animals, rain, and noble growth—the full created landscape around the camel.
terra: فَٱتَّبِعْ سَبِيلَ مَنْ أَنَابَ إِلَىَّ invites the path of voluntary return, then إِلَىَّ مَرْجِعُكُمْ states the universal return that follows regardless.
terra: The nearer punishment is made to precede ٱلْعَذَابِ ٱلْأَكْبَرِ so that people may return, linking the section's greater punishment to the still-open chance of willing return.
terra: Water is driven to barren land, crops emerge for livestock and people to eat, and the ayah asks أَفَلَا يُبْصِرُونَ, joining dry earth, food, herd, and sight.

luna: The section's food-inspection word (source root ن ظ ر) meets this verse's waiting for a meal's readiness (نَاظِرِينَ إِنَاهُ); the shared root joins looking at food to its preparation. | terra: The command not to enter the Prophet's rooms غَيْرَ نَاظِرِينَ إِنَاهُ brings looking or waiting, food, its moment of ripeness, a room, and the Prophet's proper place into one scene.
terra: Their faces are turned about in the Fire while they regret not obeying God and the Messenger, joining face, fire, and rejected message.
luna: The section's mountain image meets its secondary return root here: mountains are commanded to join David in praise, using the A-W-B root.

luna: Winds and rain revive a dead land, “thus the resurrection”; this directly repeats the section's movement from soil's revival to human resurrection. | terra: Wind, cloud, and rain revive dead land, and كَذَٰلِكَ ٱلنُّشُورُ explicitly names that scene as the likeness of resurrection.
terra: God writes what people sent ahead and their traces and has enumerated everything in a clear register, joining labor, record, and divine count.

luna: Dead earth revived with grain for eating joins the section's soil-to-resurrection proof to its questions about food and creation. | terra: Dead earth is a sign: God revives it and brings grain from it for people to eat, joining resurrection evidence directly to food.
luna: Gardens of palms and vines with springs extend the same earth-revival sign into garden provision, matching the section's flowing spring and fruit.
luna: The fruit is food from gardens people did not make, a specific reminder that the section's garden provisions are created and provided.
terra: The garden companions and spouses recline in shade upon couches, a compact parallel to the section's inhabited high room.

luna: Created livestock are placed in human possession, paralleling the section's question about how the camel was created for use. | terra: أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا أَنَّا خَلَقْنَا لَهُم... أَنْعَامًا is the closest general counterpart to looking at how the camel was created.

luna: The livestock are made subject to people for riding and food, linking the section's camel and provisions. | terra: The created livestock are made tractable, some serving as mounts and some as food, unfolding the fitting of the animal to human life.

luna: Livestock yield benefits and drink, a direct parallel to the section's animal-derived furnishing and milk scenes. | terra: Livestock provide benefits and drinks, then the passage asks whether people will give thanks, joining animal, provision, and moral sight.
terra: The purified servants sit on couches facing one another, the garden-room counterpart within the same passage that later describes Zaqqum.
terra: A cup from a flowing spring circulates among them, pairing the furnished room with its drink.
terra: The garden drink brings neither harm nor intoxication, a direct boundary against the scalding drink later in the passage.
terra: The ayah asks whether garden hospitality or the tree of Zaqqum is better, explicitly staging the two opposed provisions.
terra: Zaqqum grows from the base of Hell, making the infernal food a grotesque reversal of growth from revived earth.

luna: The section's non-nourishing thorn food has a counterpart in the tree of Zaqqum, whose fruit the damned eat and fill their bellies with. | terra: The condemned eat from it and fill their bellies, contributing the punitive meal itself.

luna: After Zaqqum, this verse gives them boiling water to drink, joining the section's failed food and tormenting drink in one scene. | terra: A mixture of boiling water follows the food, repeating the section's food-and-scalding-drink sequence.
terra: Their return is then to Hell, joining the meal to an adverse homecoming.
luna: The section says voluntary return makes one an أَوَّاب; this verse uses that label for Solomon, the servant who repeatedly turns back to God.
luna: Job is called an أَوَّاب here, another direct Quranic use of the section's word for one who willingly returns.
luna: All return to their Lord, who informs them of their deeds, matching the section's sequence of return and reckoning.
terra: Layers of fire above and below become the condemned person's shelter, the punitive inversion of roof, bedding, and room.
terra: Those who fear their Lord receive lofty chambers built above chambers with rivers below, making elevation and constructed garden space explicit.
terra: Water enters earth, varied plants grow and then dry into debris, and the process is called a reminder, connecting viewed ground to impermanence and recollection.
terra: A person tries to shield himself with his face from the worst punishment, making the face the exposed boundary of the fire scene.
terra: The Book is sent down in truth for people; guidance or loss returns to each person, while the Prophet is not their trustee.

luna: This verse tells people to turn to their Lord before punishment arrives; it clarifies the section's contrast between voluntary return and the return that follows turning away. | terra: وَأَنِيبُوا إِلَىٰ رَبِّكُمْ calls for willing return before punishment arrives, illuminating the section's difference between becoming an evvâb now and being returned later.
terra: The Day of Resurrection displays those who lied about God with blackened faces, another judgment visibly written on faces.
terra: At Judgment the earth shines, the record is placed, messengers and witnesses are brought, and God judges truly, distinguishing delivery from judgment.
terra: Every soul is paid in full for what it did, and God knows deeds best, completing the accounting scene.
terra: God makes earth a settled place, heaven a structure, forms people well, and gives good provision, gathering room, creation, and sustenance.
terra: God makes livestock so that some are ridden and some eaten, a direct account of the created fitness contemplated in the camel.
terra: Their benefits, transport of needs, and pairing with ships extend the camel scene into travel and provision.
terra: After those livestock uses God shows His signs and asks which signs people deny, matching the interrogative force of the section's look.

luna: As the section says, land revived after drying demonstrates resurrection; this verse says its reviver will surely revive the dead. | terra: The section cites the revived earth as proof of resurrection; this ayah states that the One who gives the humbled earth life gives the dead life.
terra: The Arabic Quran is revealed so the Prophet may warn of the unquestioned Gathering Day, when one group is in the garden and another in the blaze.
terra: The condemned are shown to the Fire, humbled by abasement and looking with a furtive glance, joining fire, lowered stance, and diminished sight.

luna: This verse likewise says the Messenger is not a keeper over those who turn away; his charge is only conveyance, matching the section's limit on prophetic control. | terra: If they turn away, the Prophet was not sent as their guardian; his task is only conveyance, the same division of labor as reminder versus حساب.
terra: Earth is made a cradle and roads are placed in it so people may be guided, joining spread ground to purposeful travel.

luna: Measured rain revives a dead town, “thus you will be brought forth”; the verse makes the section's water-and-resurrection correspondence explicit. | terra: Measured water revives a dead land and كَذَٰلِكَ تُخْرَجُونَ turns that earthly change into the reader's own promised emergence.
terra: God creates all pairs and provides ships and livestock for people to ride, locating the mount within the created order.
terra: Settling on the mounts' backs prompts remembrance of the One who subjected them, turning the journeying animal into recollection.
terra: وَإِنَّا إِلَىٰ رَبِّنَا لَمُنقَلِبُونَ makes every mounted journey rehearse the final return to the Lord.

luna: Gold platters and cups circulate in the garden, a specific parallel to the section's cups set out among its furnishings. | terra: Golden trays and cups circulate while souls and eyes receive what delights them, joining vessel, desire, and sight in the garden.
terra: God hears secret and private speech while His messengers with them write it, another exact meeting of hearing and record.

luna: Zaqqum is introduced as food in the punishment scene, a specific parallel to the section's thorny, unsatisfying food. | terra: The tree of Zaqqum is called the sinner's food, giving another concrete counterpart to the thorn food that cannot nourish.
luna: This verse identifies Zaqqum as the sinner's food, directly extending the section's scene of food that cannot nourish.

luna: The punishment's Zaqqum fruit is like molten metal boiling in bellies, intensifying the section's fiery food-and-drink image. | terra: That food boils inside bellies like molten metal, carrying kitchen language into punishment as the section does.

luna: This completes the boiling image with a comparison to boiling water, parallel to the section's scalding drink. | terra: كَغَلْىِ ٱلْحَمِيمِ completes the cooking comparison with boiling water, joining food's ripeness to the infernal drink.
luna: The sinner is seized and dragged to the middle of the Fire, continuing the section's forced punishment scene.
luna: Boiling water is poured over the sinner's head, a direct counterpart to the section's hot spring and fire.
terra: The God-fearing occupy a secure station, the favorable dwelling opposite the preceding Zaqqum and boiling-water scene.
terra: Gardens and springs furnish that secure station with the same paired setting as the section's high garden.
terra: They wear fine silk and face one another, making the garden an inhabited room of ease after the infernal cooking imagery.
luna: Rain as provision revives earth after death; this verse groups that sign with winds and alternation of night and day, echoing the section's creation-based reminder.
terra: Every community is seen kneeling and summoned to its record, placing bodily lowering and accounting in the same Judgment scene.
terra: God's book speaks truth because He had deeds copied, explaining who actually keeps the lines and count.
terra: Creating heaven and earth without weariness establishes God's power to revive the dead, making the viewed construction proof of the Day.

luna: The section's flowing spring and drink are set against Hell's boiling water; this verse places pure garden rivers beside a drink of boiling water. | terra: Paradise's unspoiled water and milk are set against boiling water that cuts the bowels, expanding the section's opposed drink rooms.

luna: The verse commands people to look at the built and adorned sky, closely matching the section's repeated “look how it was made” appeal. | terra: أَفَلَمْ يَنظُرُوا إِلَى ٱلسَّمَاءِ asks people to look at how heaven was built, adorned, and left without fissures, almost exactly the visual stance of 88:17-18.

luna: This continues the created-sky appeal with spread earth, firmly set mountains, and paired growth, matching the section's landscape sequence. | terra: The earth is spread and mountains cast into it after the command to inspect heaven, continuing the same downward movement of the gaze.

luna: The section joins the earth's revival to the garden; this verse sends blessed water that grows gardens and harvested grain. | terra: Blessed water descends from heaven and grows gardens and grain, the life-giving counterpart to the boiling spring of the first half.
luna: The next verse names tall palm trees with clustered fruit, extending 50:9's rain-grown provision that echoes the section's food and garden.

luna: This passage culminates in reviving a dead town and says “thus is the emergence,” the same soil-to-resurrection proof the section draws. | terra: Rain is provision for servants, revives a dead land, and is followed by كَذَٰلِكَ ٱلْخُرُوجُ, explicitly turning viewed earth into proof of emergence from graves.

luna: Two recorders sit on the right and left, giving a concrete account-keeping scene behind the section's claim that the Messenger is not the keeper. | terra: The two receivers sit right and left to receive, locating the agents who keep the record that the Prophet does not control.

luna: No word is spoken without a watcher ready to record it, joining the section's silence about idle speech to its reckoning and record. | terra: No spoken word is uttered without a watcher ready, bringing speech, hearing, and registration into a single act.
terra: The garden is promised لِكُلِّ أَوَّابٍ حَفِيظٍ, naming the voluntary returner as the one welcomed into the favorable room.
terra: The evvâb is one who feared the Merciful unseen and came with a penitent heart, connecting accepted reminder, fear, and willing inward return.

luna: Like the section's “you are only a reminder, not a controller,” this verse says the Messenger is no compeller and commands him to remind by the Quran. | terra: The Prophet is not a compeller over them; فَذَكِّرْ بِٱلْقُرْءَانِ مَن يَخَافُ وَعِيدِ gives the same bounded reminder and fear-responsive audience as 88:21-22.

luna: The section pairs raised couches with a raised sky; this verse says God built the heaven with might and is expanding it. | terra: The heaven is built with power immediately before earth is spread in 51:48, supplying the roof above that furnished floor.

luna: This verse says earth was spread (فَرَشْنَاهَا), giving the section's spread carpets and flattened ground a creation-level counterpart. | terra: وَٱلْأَرْضَ فَرَشْنَاهَا describes earth as something spread like bedding, making the world's floor the analogue of the garden's laid furnishings.
terra: وَكِتَابٍ مَّسْطُورٍ names an inscribed book with the same line-writing field the section associates with مُصَيْطِر.
terra: The inscribed book of 52:2 is فِى رَقٍّ مَّنشُورٍ, an opened or spread parchment that distinguishes the record's surface from what is written on it.
terra: وَٱلسَّقْفِ ٱلْمَرْفُوعِ turns the raised heaven into a lifted roof, directly supporting the section's world-as-room meeting.
terra: Garden dwellers are told to eat and drink pleasantly for what they used to do, joining fulfilled labor with nourishing provision.

luna: This garden has couches arranged in rows (سُرُرٍ مَّصْفُوفَةٍ), meeting the section's arranged pillows and spread furnishings. | terra: عَلَىٰ سُرُرٍ مَّصْفُوفَةٍ combines the section's raised couches with its things arranged in rows in one garden furnishing.

luna: The section's placed cups and unheard idle speech meet here: cups are passed around, with no لَغْو or sin in the garden. | terra: A cup circulates in the garden with no لَغْوٌ and no sin around it, uniting the section's cups and absence of empty speech.
luna: This continues 52:23's garden cups and speech with servants circulating among them, adding the service surrounding the section's set-out vessels.
terra: The question أَمْ هُمُ ٱلْمُصَيْطِرُونَ uses the controlling sense of the same word, clarifying by contrast what the Prophet is denied in 88:22.

luna: The section contrasts toil with being satisfied by one's striving; this verse states that a person has only what he strives for (مَا سَعَىٰ). | terra: A human being has only what he strove for, isolating the same سَعْي whose outcome divides the two groups of faces.

luna: The section's labor and satisfaction meet the claim that one's striving will be seen (سَوْفَ يُرَىٰ), before recompense. | terra: That striving will be seen, bringing labor itself under the gaze before recompense.

luna: The section's final account and the face satisfied with its effort meet the promise of full recompense (الْجَزَاءَ الْأَوْفَىٰ). | terra: The striving is then repaid with the fullest repayment, completing the movement from work to account.
terra: With eyes humbled, people emerge from graves like scattered locusts, directly joining lowered gaze to resurrection from the ground.
terra: They are dragged on their faces into the Fire and told to taste its touch, combining the lowered face with burning punishment.
terra: Everything people did is فِى ٱلزُّبُرِ; 54:53 then says every small and great thing is inscribed, joining labor to record.

luna: The section connects its word مُصَيْطِر (from س ط ر) with the record; here every small and great thing is مُسْتَطَر, written down. | terra: وَكُلُّ صَغِيرٍ وَكَبِيرٍ مُّسْتَطَرٌ makes every small and great thing an inscribed line, supplying the record sense the section hears inside مُصَيْطِر.

luna: The section meets the raised couches and spread rugs with creation's raised heaven (رَفَعَهَا) and established balance. | terra: وَٱلسَّمَاءَ رَفَعَهَا places the raised heaven beside the divinely set balance, linking physical elevation to the just measure culminating in حساب.

luna: The earth is laid out for creatures, echoing the section's flattened ground as the world's habitable floor beneath the garden's furnished room. | terra: وَٱلْأَرْضَ وَضَعَهَا لِلْأَنَامِ answers the raised sky of 55:7 with earth laid down, using the room-making motion heard in the section's placed cups and spread floor.
terra: The condemned circle between Hell and حَمِيمٍ آنٍ, using the same peak-heated sense as the section's spring already brought to its final boil.
luna: Two garden springs flow here, a relief-bearing counterpart to the section's boiling spring and a parallel to its running garden spring.

luna: The couches are lined with brocade and their fruit is near, adding textile and provision details to the section's furnished garden room. | terra: The garden dwellers recline on couches lined with brocade, another room whose unseen inner furnishing exceeds its visible surface.

luna: Green cushions and fine carpets here furnish a garden scene, directly meeting the section's cushions, carpets, and furnished room. | terra: They recline upon green cushions and fine carpets, directly repeating the section's paired cushion-and-carpet furnishings.
terra: خَافِضَةٌ رَّافِعَةٌ says the Event lowers and raises, gathering the section's lowered and delighted faces, raised heaven and couches, and final reversal of rank.

luna: The garden's couches are richly woven, a direct furnishing parallel to the section's raised seats and arranged pillows. | terra: The companions are عَلَىٰ سُرُرٍ مَّوْضُونَةٍ, another direct formulation of the garden's prepared couches.

luna: The residents recline face to face on those couches, adding a specific posture to the section's furnished garden scene. | terra: They recline facing one another on those couches, supplying the lived posture of the furnished room.
terra: Cups, pitchers, and a goblet from a flowing spring reproduce the garden inventory of vessel and running source.

luna: The section says no idle word is heard in the garden; this verse says its people hear neither لَغْو nor sin there. | terra: لَا يَسْمَعُونَ فِيهَا لَغْوًا repeats both the hearing and the excluded empty speech of 88:11.
terra: Only repeated words of peace are heard there, stating what replaces the excluded لَغْو in 56:25.
luna: This begins the opposite outcome to the section's punished group: the people of the right are in a garden of ease.
luna: The garden's lote trees are stripped of thorns, a precise reversal of the section's thorny darī as food that cannot nourish.
luna: Bananas layered with fruit add to 56:28's thorn-free garden provision, a specific abundance opposite the section's hunger and darī.
luna: Extended shade here answers the section's blazing punishment with a garden scene of shelter and relief.
luna: A flowing spring here directly answers the section's hot spring and matches its garden's running spring.
luna: Abundant fruit in the garden reverses the section's meager, unsatisfying food.
luna: The fruit is neither cut off nor forbidden, the inverse of the section's food that cannot satisfy hunger.

luna: The garden's raised couches (فُرُشٍ مَّرْفُوعَةٍ) meet the section's elevated couches and its image of furnishing the garden room. | terra: وَفُرُشٍ مَّرْفُوعَةٍ brings spread bedding and elevation into one phrase, exactly meeting the section's raised furniture and spread carpets.
luna: This continues the elevated garden bedding with newly created companions, completing the garden's furnished comfort around the section's couches.

luna: The section's hot fire and drink have a parallel punishment: the left-hand company is in scorching wind and boiling water (سَمُومٍ وَحَمِيمٍ). | terra: The companions of the left dwell amid scorching wind and boiling water, an infernal climate opposite the high garden's spring.

luna: This continues 56:42's punishment with a shade of black smoke, the inverse of the section's high garden and its comfortable furnishings. | terra: Their shade is black smoke, making the promised room itself a dark covering.

luna: The continuation says that shade is neither cool nor beneficial, reversing the section's running spring and garden comfort. | terra: The smoky shade is neither cool nor pleasant, spelling out the failed shelter begun in 56:43.

luna: This verse gives the left-hand group's food as Zaqqum, a parallel to the section's thorny food in Hell. | terra: The companions of the left eat from the tree of Zaqqum, another sterile hell food placed before the camel-like drinking in 56:55.
luna: They fill their bellies with that tree's fruit, sharpening the contrast with the section's food that cannot satisfy hunger.

luna: They drink boiling water after the tree's fruit, joining the section's unsatisfying food and scalding drink. | terra: They drink boiling water after filling their bellies, directly joining hell food and the scalding drink of the section.

luna: The drinkers gulp like thirsty camels, joining the section's singled-out camel with its contrast between easy milk and tormenting drink. | terra: فَشَارِبُونَ شُرْبَ ٱلْهِيمِ makes the condemned drink like desperately thirsty camels, bringing camel and hell drink into one explicit image.
luna: The verse calls this their welcome on the Day of Judgment, turning garden hospitality into punishment.
terra: أَفَرَءَيْتُمُ ٱلْمَاءَ ٱلَّذِى تَشْرَبُونَ turns drinking water into an object of directed sight, joining the section's visual and drinking vocabularies.
terra: The question whether people sent water from the cloud or God did locates the hidden giver behind the visible provision.
terra: God could make that water bitter, marking the boundary between gracious drink and the punitive drink of boiling springs.

luna: This concise formulation says God gives life to earth after its death, directly restating the section's soil-and-resurrection link. | terra: God gives earth life after its death and explains the signs so people may understand, making visible revival an intelligible proof.
terra: Nearer life is rain-grown vegetation that delights observers and then withers into debris, while the Hereafter holds punishment or lasting forgiveness and pleasure.
terra: God has counted the deeds people forgot and will report them at resurrection, separating human forgetfulness from divine accounting.
terra: The Creator of the layered heavens commands the beholder to return sight and ask whether any fissure is visible, closely matching the question that directs sight to creation.
terra: Repeated sight returns خَاسِئًا وَهُوَ حَسِيرٌ, making the very eye that examines the raised heaven come back humbled and exhausted like the section's low, laboring face.
terra: Those cast into Hell hear it roaring as it boils, giving the fire itself the overwhelming soundscape.
terra: Its keepers ask each group whether no warner came, linking that heard fire to the rejected messenger who had only to warn.
terra: When the promised event is seen near, the disbelievers' faces become distressed, joining sight, face, and the arrival they denied.
terra: The call to prostrate and their inability to do so begins the scene completed by humbled eyes in 68:43, marking the point when willing bowing is no longer possible.

luna: The section's humbly lowered faces become forced abasement here: eyes are خَاشِعَة and humiliation overwhelms them when they are called to prostrate. | terra: Their eyes are خَاشِعَةً and abasement covers them because they once declined the call to prostrate; compulsory lowering answers the section's missed voluntary lowering.
luna: Earth and mountains are lifted and crushed on the Day, reversing the section's spread earth and erected mountains.
luna: The sky splits on that Day, a specific reversal of the section's raised and constructed heaven.

luna: A person receives his record in his right hand, meeting the section's final account and clarifying how one outcome is assessed. | terra: Receiving the record in the right hand begins the sequence whose speaker joyfully says in 69:20 that he expected his account.

luna: The person knows he will meet his account, a direct articulation of the section's return followed by reckoning. | terra: The garden-bound person says he knew he would meet his حساب, placing confident anticipation immediately before the high garden.
luna: The right-hand recipient is in a pleasing life, a counterpart to the section's faces satisfied with their effort and garden ease.

luna: “An elevated garden” (جَنَّةٍ عَالِيَةٍ) here exactly meets the section's high garden and gives the favorable account its setting. | terra: فِى جَنَّةٍ عَالِيَةٍ exactly repeats the high garden that receives the satisfied face.
luna: This continues 69:22's elevated garden with fruit clusters close at hand, adding garden provision to the section's high room and set food.

luna: They are told to eat and drink pleasantly for what they sent ahead, contrasting the section's unsatisfying food with reward for effort. | terra: The people of that high garden are told to eat and drink for what they sent ahead, joining provision to accepted labor.

luna: The other recipient is handed his record in his left hand, reversing 69:19 and making the section's two final outcomes concrete. | terra: Receiving the record in the left hand begins the opposite account, matching the section's divided outcomes.

luna: He is told to read his record, completing the account scene that the section leaves to God rather than the Messenger. | terra: The condemned wishes he had never known what his حساب was, reversing the confident anticipation of 69:20.
luna: His wealth does not avail him (مَا أَغْنَىٰ عَنِّي مَالِيَهْ), paralleling the section's repeated failure of worldly sufficiency.

luna: His food is only ghislin, an explicit counterpart to the section's thorn food that neither nourishes nor satisfies hunger. | terra: وَلَا طَعَامٌ إِلَّا مِنْ غِسْلِينٍ exactly parallels the section's “no food except” construction with a second hell food.

luna: Only sinners eat that food, completing the punishment side of 69:36's failed nourishment and the section's divided outcomes. | terra: Only sinners eat that food, locating the deprivation in the adverse account begun by the left-hand record.

luna: On the promised Day eyes are humbled and humiliation covers them, matching the section's bowed faces under punishment. | terra: They emerge from graves with eyes lowered while تَرْهَقُهُمْ ذِلَّةٌ covers them, joining resurrection, gaze, and an enveloping abasement.

luna: Earth is made a spread (بِسَاطًا) here; this wording directly meets the section's spread carpets and its earth flattened as a world-floor. | terra: God makes earth بِسَاطًا, explicitly treating the terrestrial surface as a carpet.

luna: The spread earth lets people travel through broad paths, joining the section's walk from the opening arrival to the final return. | terra: That carpet enables travel through broad roads, giving the spread earth the daily journeying function evoked by the camel.
terra: In the context of messengers delivering their Lord's messages, God encompasses what is with them and counts everything, placing conveyance and final oversight in their distinct roles.
terra: Food that chokes and painful punishment give another concrete form of eating that cannot nourish or pass easily.
terra: The question asks what is wrong with them that they turn away from the reminder, joining the Prophet's message to the section's turning away.
terra: Their flight from the reminder is likened to startled wild donkeys, bringing a herd animal into the response-to-warning scene.
terra: The herd flees a lion, completing the animal movement that images rejection of the reminder.

luna: The section's two faces on that Day are elaborated as bright faces here, a specific reversal of the faces lowered in its opening scene. | terra: Some faces that Day are radiant, the positive face before the act of looking in 75:23.

luna: The bright faces of 75:22 look toward their Lord, contrasting the section's humiliated, downward-looking faces with the garden's ease. | terra: إِلَىٰ رَبِّهَا نَاظِرَةٌ makes the blessed face a looking face, answering the section's earthly command to look.

luna: This verse gives the other side of 75:22–23: faces on that Day are gloomy, matching the section's punished faces. | terra: Other faces that Day are gloomy, beginning the opposed half of the same facial diptych.

luna: Those gloomy faces expect a calamity here, completing the opposite face-scene to the section's radiant, satisfied garden faces. | terra: Those gloomy faces expect a crushing calamity, giving their expression its anticipated cause.

luna: This verse says he neither believed nor prayed (فَلَا صَدَّقَ وَلَا صَلَّىٰ); 75:32 adds the denial and turning away named in the section. | terra: فَلَا صَدَّقَ وَلَا صَلَّىٰ contributes the refused prayer; 75:32 then names the denial and turning away cited by the section.

luna: This verse's own contribution is denial and turning away (كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ); preceding 75:31 says he neither believed nor prayed, the pairing the section invokes. | terra: وَلَٰكِن كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ names denial and turning away; 75:31 supplies the refused prayer that makes this the section's bodily reversal.
luna: The righteous drink a cup mixed with camphor here, a garden drink set against the section's difficult and scalding drink.
luna: That cup comes from a spring made to flow; this joins the section's flowing garden spring and pleasant drink.

luna: The garden's residents recline without sun or bitter cold, reversing the section's burning heat and matching its furnished repose. | terra: Reclining on couches, the garden dwellers experience neither sun nor biting cold, making the room a perfected shelter.
luna: Shade closes over the garden's residents and its fruits are brought near, developing the section's comfortable garden provision.

luna: Silver vessels and cups are circulated here, a direct garden counterpart to the section's cups set out. | terra: Silver vessels and crystal cups circulate among them, repeating the placed cups of the section's garden.
luna: This verse specifies silver goblets measured to their measure, echoing the section's prepared cups and measured provision.
luna: The garden's ginger-mixed drink is pleasant, adding a specific counterpart to the section's hot, barely swallowed drink.
luna: The drink comes from a spring named Salsabil, expanding the section's garden image of a flowing spring and set cups.
terra: The revelation is a reminder, and whoever wills may take a path to his Lord, expressing the voluntary response available before final return.
terra: The condemned are ordered toward a three-branched shadow, beginning a shelter scene that reverses the garden room.
terra: That shadow neither shades nor protects from flame, explicitly turning shelter into its opposite.
terra: Hell throws sparks as large as a fortress, supplying the fiery object compared with camels in 77:33.
terra: The fire's sparks appear like yellow camels, placing the animal contemplated as a created sign inside the punitive fire scene.
terra: The God-fearing are amid shade and springs, the real shelter and drink opposite the failed shade of 77:30-31.
terra: They receive whatever fruit they desire, adding nourishing food to that shelter.
terra: The righteous are told to eat and drink pleasantly for what they used to do, another direct reversal of effort answered by food that cannot satisfy.
terra: God says He thus rewards those who do good, identifying the room, drink, and food as the result of accepted work.
terra: When told ٱرْكَعُوا they do not bow, giving the worldly refusal whose delayed bodily consequence appears in the humbled faces.

luna: The verse calls earth a resting place, making the section's worldly ground a dwelling floor and its elevated garden couches a fitting reversal. | terra: أَلَمْ نَجْعَلِ ٱلْأَرْضَ مِهَادًا presents earth as a prepared bed, another direct construction of the world's furnished room.

luna: Mountains are made pegs here; their fixed height contributes the same formed landscape as the section's invitation to look at mountains. | terra: The mountains are pegs, completing the tent-like earth image and matching the viewed mountains of 88:19.
terra: In Hell they taste neither coolness nor drink, a direct deprivation opposite the garden's running spring and cups.
terra: Only boiling water and foul fluid answer that deprivation, supplying the punitive drink itself.
terra: وَكُلَّ شَىْءٍ أَحْصَيْنَاهُ كِتَابًا makes comprehensive enumeration a book, the precise union of counting and lines.
terra: وَكَأْسًا دِهَاقًا supplies the full cup within the same passage that excludes empty speech and calls the gift sufficient.

luna: This verse repeats the section's garden silence: they hear neither idle speech (لَغْوًا) nor falsehood there. | terra: لَّا يَسْمَعُونَ فِيهَا لَغْوًا repeats the section's exact relation between garden hearing and worthless speech.
terra: عَطَاءً حِسَابًا calls the garden reward an ample or sufficient gift, realizing the section's secondary sense of the حساب root inside a reckoning passage.

luna: The section's lowered gaze recurs as eyes humbled (خَاشِعَةٌ) on the Day, here following hearts that tremble. | terra: أَبْصَارُهَا خَاشِعَةٌ gives the trembling hearts of that Day the section's exact humbled-eye posture.

luna: The verse asks whether people or heaven are harder to create, introducing 79:28's raised sky and the section's creation-based looking. | terra: The question whether humans are harder to create or heaven turns looking at the world's construction into an argument for the resurrection scene.

luna: The sky's raised ceiling here parallels 88:18's raised heaven and the section's raised couches, linking the world's construction to the garden interior. | terra: رَفَعَ سَمْكَهَا فَسَوَّاهَا says God raised and proportioned heaven's canopy, a direct parallel to the raised sky in the section.

luna: The earth is spread here after the sky is raised, the same vertical and horizontal construction the section connects to garden furnishings. | terra: وَٱلْأَرْضَ بَعْدَ ذَٰلِكَ دَحَاهَا follows the raised canopy with earth spread out, reproducing the world's roof-and-floor order.

luna: The spread earth yields its water and pasture; this completes the section's look from land and camel toward the provisions that sustain life. | terra: Water and pasture are brought from the spread earth, showing how its preparation becomes drink and food rather than the sterile provisions of punishment.

luna: Mountains are set here after earth and pasture, matching the section's sequence of looking at sky, mountains, and earth as formed things. | terra: The mountains are fixed after heaven and earth, completing the same created landscape shown in 88:18-20.
terra: مَتَاعًا لَّكُمْ وَلِأَنْعَامِكُمْ makes that landscape provision for people and livestock, bringing the viewed camel back into the creation sequence.
terra: The passage is declared a reminder, defining the report's function rather than coercive control.
terra: فَمَن شَاءَ ذَكَرَهُ leaves remembering to whoever wills, marking the hearer's voluntary response.

luna: The section explicitly joins the camel's food scene to the call “let the human look at his food” (فَلْيَنظُرِ الْإِنسَانُ إِلَىٰ طَعَامِهِ). | terra: فَلْيَنظُرِ ٱلْإِنسَانُ إِلَىٰ طَعَامِهِ repeats the section's summons to look, now directing sight to food rather than the camel.

luna: The section's invitation to look at food continues into this verse: God pours water down, supplying the food whose origins the next lines reveal. | terra: After the command to inspect food, poured water begins its making, the nourishing opposite of water poured or offered as punishment.

luna: This continues 80:24's food inspection with the splitting of earth; the section also makes earth's surface part of what the eye must consider. | terra: ثُمَّ شَقَقْنَا ٱلْأَرْضَ شَقًّا opens the earth so food can grow, showing the prepared ground beneath the visual command.
luna: The food inspection of 80:24 continues with grain grown from the split earth, identifying what that looking reveals.
luna: This continuation names grapes and fodder, linking the earth's growth to food for people and animals.
luna: Olives and date palms continue the food inventory that follows the section's call to inspect one's food.
luna: Dense gardens extend the food-and-earth scene after 80:24's invitation to look at food.

luna: Fruit and pasture continue the provision scene, joining the section's garden food to the camel's earthly nourishment. | terra: Fruit and pasture stand among the foods produced, directly opposing the sterile thorn that neither fattens nor ends hunger.

luna: The produce is provision for people and livestock, completing the food list that links the section's camel, earth, and eating. | terra: مَّتَاعًا لَّكُمْ وَلِأَنْعَامِكُمْ makes the food scene provision for people and their livestock, returning the gaze from food to the camel.

luna: The section distinguishes faces by their fate; this verse pictures faces on that Day radiant and rejoicing, the garden side of that contrast. | terra: Some faces that Day are radiant, beginning the same division of eschatological faces as the section.
luna: This completes 80:38's joyful faces and reinforces the section's contrast between the two groups' faces on the Day.

luna: The opposing faces are dusty here, a dry-earth and humiliation image that recalls the section's lowered, punished faces. | terra: Other faces that Day have dust upon them, making the earth itself the visible ground of the abased face.

luna: Darkness covers those dusty faces, completing a face-covering scene opposite the section's soft, contented faces. | terra: تَرْهَقُهَا قَتَرَةٌ says darkness covers those dusty faces, completing the section's cover-on-face image.
luna: Mountains are moved away on the Hour, reversing the section's view of them firmly set in the created landscape.
luna: A pregnant she-camel is abandoned when the Hour arrives; this is a specific inversion of the section's useful, observed camel, though the link is distant.
terra: When the scrolls are laid open, the act of spreading becomes the disclosure of recorded labor.
terra: When Hell is set ablaze, the punitive room is made present in the same final unveiling as the opened records.
terra: When the garden is brought near, the favorable room directly answers the blaze of 81:12.
terra: Every soul then knows what it has brought, resolving record, fire, and garden into the result of its own work.
terra: Guardians are appointed over people, distinguishing the true overseers from the Messenger who is not مُصَيْطِر.
terra: Those guardians are noble writers, identifying supervision specifically as inscription.
terra: They know what people do, joining human labor to the divinely assigned record.
terra: The wicked person's record is in Sijjin, beginning the recorded opposite of the garden-facing couch scene later in the surah.
terra: كِتَابٌ مَّرْقُومٌ specifies that adverse destiny as an inscribed record.
terra: The righteous person's record is in Illiyyin, supplying the elevated recorded counterpart to Sijjin.
terra: كِتَابٌ مَّرْقُومٌ repeats the inscribed-record formula for the righteous before their bliss and looking from couches.
terra: عَلَى ٱلْأَرَائِكِ يَنظُرُونَ places looking upon garden couches, precisely joining the world's commanded gaze to the room it prefigures.
terra: The radiance of bliss is recognized in their faces, completing the couch-and-gaze scene with the section's softened happy face.
terra: عَلَى ٱلْأَرَائِكِ يَنظُرُونَ is repeated after the reversal of mockery, making the final gaze itself part of recompense.

luna: The section's toil, return, and account are staged as labor toward the Lord and a meeting with Him (كَادِحٌ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ ... فَمُلَاقِيهِ). | terra: Humanity labors painfully toward the Lord and will meet Him, joining exhausting work to the inevitable return.

luna: This verse gives the person whose record is handed rightward an easy account, making the section's final حساب a favorable reckoning for one outcome. | terra: Receiving the record in the right hand begins the favorable result of that labor.

luna: The section's account is illuminated by this verse's easy reckoning (حِسَابًا يَسِيرًا), one favorable outcome of the final reckoning. | terra: فَسَوْفَ يُحَاسَبُ حِسَابًا يَسِيرًا promises an easy accounting, giving one end of the section's measure of sufficiency.

luna: The easy-account recipient returns to his people rejoicing, matching the section's return and the garden face pleased with its outcome. | terra: He returns joyfully to his people after the easy account, joining reckoning, happy face, and return.

luna: The other account recipient is given his record from behind his back, reversing the favorable reckoning of the section's garden group. | terra: Receiving the record behind one's back opens the adverse counterpart to the right-hand record of 84:7.

luna: He calls for destruction after receiving that record, completing the section's contrast between contented and humiliated faces. | terra: That person calls for destruction rather than returning joyfully, giving the emotional outcome of the adverse record.

luna: He enters blazing fire, completing 84:10–11's adverse account and echoing the section's hot punishment. | terra: He enters a blazing fire, completing the labor-to-record-to-fire sequence opposite 84:7-9.
terra: When the Quran is recited they do not prostrate, setting heard revelation and refused lowering against the posture of Judgment.
terra: فَذَكِّرْ إِن نَّفَعَتِ ٱلذِّكْرَىٰ repeats the command to remind while leaving reception outside the reminder's control.
terra: سَيَذَّكَّرُ مَن يَخْشَىٰ identifies the one who fears as the hearer who accepts that reminder.
terra: The most wretched enters ٱلنَّارَ ٱلْكُبْرَىٰ, closely answering the section's heated fire and greater punishment.
terra: He neither dies there nor lives, spelling out the impossible condition behind the drink from which death approaches on every side.
luna: The peaceful soul offers another face of the section's satisfied outcome before its return to God and entry into the garden.

luna: The soul is told to return to its Lord pleased and pleasing, a direct parallel to the section's satisfied face and final return. | terra: ٱرْجِعِى إِلَىٰ رَبِّكِ رَاضِيَةً مَّرْضِيَّةً is a welcomed and mutually pleasing return, the blessed opposite of the compulsory return of those who turn their backs.
luna: The returning soul is welcomed among God's servants, completing 89:28's return as a communal garden entry beside the section's garden gathering.
luna: The returned soul is told to enter Paradise, completing the section's link between return and the high garden.
terra: عَلَيْهِمْ نَارٌ مُّؤْصَدَةٌ makes fire close over them, another direct union of covering and flame.
terra: The oath by heaven and what built it repeats the section's question about how the sky was raised and made.
terra: The paired oath by earth and what spread it repeats the downward movement from constructed heaven to prepared ground.
terra: إِنَّ سَعْيَكُمْ لَشَتَّىٰ states that human striving diverges, supplying a compact key to the two opposite outcomes of effort in the section.
terra: Giving and fearing God begin the path whose striving is eased toward ease.
terra: فَسَنُيَسِّرُهُ لِلْيُسْرَىٰ names the favorable destination of that striving.
terra: Withholding and considering oneself self-sufficient begin the reversed path, pointedly misusing the notion of sufficiency.
terra: فَسَنُيَسِّرُهُ لِلْعُسْرَىٰ gives the adverse destination of the self-sufficient person's striving.
terra: Only the most wretched enters the blazing fire, preparing the denial-and-turning explanation in the next ayah.
terra: ٱلَّذِى كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ exactly joins denial and turning away as the path to that blaze.
terra: إِنَّ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ ٱلرُّجْعَىٰ states the same inescapable direction as 88:25 immediately after describing human transgression.
luna: Every atom's weight of good will be seen, specifying the small-scale measure behind the section's work and final account.
luna: Every atom's weight of evil will likewise be seen, completing the section's account of both outcomes.
terra: إِنَّهَا عَلَيْهِم مُّؤْصَدَةٌ likewise describes the kindled fire as shut upon them, turning enclosure itself into punishment.
